rationale: Read all sections, the registry code, the six-row gate table, the five-frame trace, the MCP error table and version paragraph. Checked against the 2026-07-28 tools page: inputSchema MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (not null); protocol errors (unknown tool, malformed request, server error) are JSON-RPC errors clients MAY pass to the model; tool execution errors (API, input validation, business logic) use isError:true and clients SHOULD pass them; servers MUST validate inputs, apply access controls, rate limit and sanitize outputs; clients MUST treat annotations as untrusted unless from trusted servers and SHOULD show inputs. Versioning page: _meta per-request version, UnsupportedProtocolVersionError -32022 listing supported versions, client SHOULD retry with a mutual version or surface an error; legacy 2025-11-25 SHOULD disconnect. typeof null is object per MDN, so the null-as-type-failure rule is correct. Mapping unknown_tool to protocol error and invalid_arguments/tool_failed to execution errors matches the spec lists. Wording 4: several hedged paragraphs (decoder/framework callout, compatibility callout) are dense and partly repeat each other; no factual defect.
